summary: Checkpoint 1 of the R14.3 part (Claude Code cc-39fac3), under the accepted RS-06, from Conrad's appendix to Ribet–Stein (The Shimura construction in weight 2). R14.5: the modular abelian variety A_f = J₁(N)/p_f J₁(N), Shimura's dimension theorem, differentials, the J₀(N) version and the nonconstant Abel–Jacobi composite (oldform multiplicity planned, primary source unread). R14.6: Hecke operators on the Néron model, the Eichler–Shimura relation and cusp-normalised Abel–Jacobi maps. R14.3: the weight-two Betti inputs (Shimura isomorphism, pairings, rank-two freeness). R14.4 not read.

nodes.title: The weight-two Shimura isomorphism is Hecke-equivariant
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 5, the Hodge decomposition gives S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) ⊕ S̄₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) ≅ H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) ⊗ ℂ, and it identifies ⟨n⟩ ⊕ ⟨n⟩̄ with ⟨n⟩^*, T_p ⊕ T̄_p with T_p^* = (π₁^{(p)})_* ∘ (π₂^{(p)})^* and w_N ⊕ w̄_N with w^*_{e^{2πi/N}}, where π₁^{(p)}, π₂^{(p)} : X₁(N, p) → X₁(N) are the degeneracy maps and (π₁^{(p)})_* is the trace.
hypotheses: N ≥ 5 (for N < 5 both sides vanish); the Betti-side integral structure is Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8's modular-symbol lattice, whose comparison with H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) is part of this stage.
proofSteps: Hodge decomposition of the compact Riemann surface X₁(N)^an with H⁰(Ω¹) = S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ).
Compute T_p^* on H¹ through the trace along π₁^{(p)} (stalkwise sum with ramification multiplicities) and pullback along π₂^{(p)}; compare with the double-coset action on cusp forms.
Diamond operators and w_ζ are induced by automorphisms, so pullback commutes with the Hodge decomposition.
acceptance: Conrad omits the proof of the compatibility; a complete proof must check the trace formula against the classical double coset (ModularCurvesPartII R12.5 normalises the differentials and Hecke operators).

nodes.title: Cup product and the Petersson product
nodes.statement: With H²(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) ≅ ℤ by the i-orientation, the cup product pairing on H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) and the non-normalised Petersson product satisfy (Sh(f₁ + ḡ₁), Sh(f₂ + ḡ₂)) = 4π(⟨f₁, g₂⟩ − ⟨f₂, g₁⟩).
hypotheses: The cup-product pairing is perfect; the Petersson integral converges by exponential decay at the cusps.
proofSteps: Represent classes by harmonic 1-forms f dz + ḡ dz̄ and compute ∫ α ∧ β with dz ∧ dz̄ = −2i dx dy.
acceptance: Only adjoints matter downstream; the factor 4π is harmless.

sources.locator: Appendix by B. Conrad, p. 66 (printed page; PDF page 70)

nodes.title: Hecke operators are self-adjoint for the w_ζ-twisted pairing
nodes.statement: With [x, y] = (x, w^*_ζ y) for ζ = e^{2πi/N}, every T ∈ T₁(N) is self-adjoint on H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ); for (·,·) the adjoint of T_p^* (p ∤ N) is ⟨p⁻¹⟩^* T_p^* and that of ⟨n⟩^* is ⟨n⁻¹⟩^*. The same holds for any primitive N-th root ζ.
hypotheses: T₁(N) ⊂ End_ℤ H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) generated by the T_p^* and ⟨n⟩^*; commutative and finite flat over ℤ (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8 owns the integral Hecke algebra).
proofSteps: Transport the classical Petersson adjoints (T_p for p | N via w_N) through cup-product-petersson.
w^*_{ζ^j} ∘ w^*_ζ = ⟨j⟩^*, a unit commuting with T₁(N), reduces general ζ to e^{2πi/N}.
acceptance: The case T = T_p^* with p | N is the subtle one; keep it.

sources.locator: Appendix by B. Conrad, p. 66 (printed page; PDF page 70)

nodes.title: H¹ is free of rank two over the Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℚ) is free of rank 2 over ℚ ⊗ T₁(N), and Hom_ℚ(ℚ ⊗ T₁(N), ℚ) is free of rank 1 (ℚ ⊗ T₁(N) is Gorenstein). Consequently V_ℓ(N) = ℚ_ℓ ⊗ T_ℓ(J₁(N)) is free of rank 2 over ℚ_ℓ ⊗ T₁(N) for either Hecke action.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero coefficients; integral freeness is not claimed (it can fail at Eisenstein maximal ideals).
proofSteps: Self-duality H¹ ≅ Hom(H¹, ℚ) as ℚ ⊗ T-modules via [·,·].
Semilocal: local freeness of constant rank is free; check after base change to ℂ.
The pairing S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) × (ℂ ⊗ T₁(N)) → ℂ, (f, T) ↦ a₁(Tf) is perfect (a₁(T_n f) = a_n(f) and T ↪ End S₂), so S₂ is free of rank 1 over ℂ ⊗ T and H¹ ⊗ ℂ = S₂ ⊕ S̄₂ is free of rank 2.
acceptance: Integral freeness after localising at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal is a separate statement (remaining work).

nodes.title: The Hecke prime and coefficient field of a newform
nodes.statement: For a newform f ∈ S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ), K_f ⊂ ℂ is the number field generated by the a_p(f), p ∤ N (it contains all a_n(f) and the values of the character χ_f), and p_f = ker(T₁(N) → K_f, T ↦ eigenvalue of T on f) is a minimal prime of T₁(N) with (T₁(N)/p_f) ⊗ ℚ ≅ K_f.
hypotheses: f a normalised newform of weight 2 and level exactly N (Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 4).
proofSteps: The eigenvalue map T₁(N) → ℂ has image the order ℤ[a_n(f)] ⊂ K_f; its kernel is prime.
Minimality: T₁(N) ⊗ ℚ is reduced on the newform part (multiplicity one), so p_f is minimal.
acceptance: Weak multiplicity one gives a_n(f) ∈ K_f for all n.

nodes.title: The modular abelian variety A_f
nodes.statement: A_f := J₁(N)/p_f J₁(N), the quotient of the Jacobian J₁(N) = Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/ℚ} by the abelian subvariety generated by the images of the elements of p_f (acting through the Picard action). It is an abelian variety over ℚ with good reduction over ℤ[1/N], with an action of T₁(N)/p_f, hence of K_f in the isogeny category. For trivial χ_f, A_f is isogenous to the analogous quotient of J₀(N) (trivial-character-J0).
hypotheses: Convention: Conrad takes the Picard ( )^* action of T₁(N) on Pic⁰; Ribet–Stein take the quotient by the image of the annihilator of f in T; the two give isogenous quotients.
proofSteps: Form the abelian subvariety Σ_{t ∈ p_f} t(J₁(N)) (finitely many generators of p_f suffice) and take the quotient abelian variety over ℚ (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2).
Good reduction over ℤ[1/N]: J₁(N) is the Néron model of an abelian scheme over ℤ[1/N] and quotients of abelian schemes by abelian subschemes are abelian schemes (or Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich).
acceptance: A_f is nonzero when f exists (modular-quotient-dimension).
Do not assert a quotient of a modular-curve Jacobian for weight > 2.

nodes.title: Tate modules of quotients
nodes.statement: For an exact sequence B′ → B → A → 0 of abelian varieties over a field of characteristic prime to ℓ, the sequence V_ℓ(B′) → V_ℓ(B) → V_ℓ(A) → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: Rational Tate modules; integrally the sequence can fail to be exact.
proofSteps: Reduce to an algebraically closed field; by Poincaré complete reducibility B is isogenous to (image of B′) × A′ with A′ → A an isogeny; isogenies induce isomorphisms on V_ℓ.
acceptance: Test: an isogeny B → A with kernel of order ℓ is surjective on V_ℓ but not on T_ℓ.

nodes.title: Shimura's theorem: dim A_f = [K_f : ℚ]
nodes.statement: dim A_f = [K_f : ℚ], and V_ℓ(A_f) = V_ℓ(J₁(N))/p_f V_ℓ(J₁(N)) is free of rank 2 over ℚ_ℓ ⊗_ℚ K_f. In particular A_f ≠ 0 and dim V_ℓ(A_f) = 2[K_f : ℚ].
hypotheses: The Frobenius characteristic polynomial on V_ℓ(A_f) is AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1/R19.6's statement, not a defining property of A_f.
proofSteps: V_ℓ(J₁(N)) is free of rank 2 over ℚ_ℓ ⊗ T₁(N) (betti-free-rank-two).
quotient-tate-exact applied to p_f J₁(N) → J₁(N) → A_f → 0 identifies V_ℓ(A_f) with V_ℓ(J₁(N))/p_f.
Hence V_ℓ(A_f) is free of rank 2 over ℚ_ℓ ⊗ T₁(N)/p_f = ℚ_ℓ ⊗ K_f, of ℚ_ℓ-dimension 2[K_f : ℚ] = 2 dim A_f.

nodes.title: Differentials on A_f
nodes.statement: Pullback along J₁(N) → A_f identifies H⁰(A_f, Ω¹) ⊗ ℂ with the span of the Galois conjugates f^σ (σ : K_f ↪ ℂ) in S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) = Cot₀(J₁(N)_ℂ), when T₁(N) acts on J₁(N) through the Albanese action (T_p)_*, whose cotangent action is the classical one; with the Picard action T_p^* the image is w_ζ of that span.
hypotheses: Conrad's warning: the Picard action on Cot₀ is the Petersson adjoint of the classical action; w_ζ conjugates one action into the other.
proofSteps: Cot₀(A_f) ↪ Cot₀(J₁(N)) is the subspace killed by p_f for the induced action on cotangent spaces.
For the Albanese action this is the classical action; the p_f-eigenspace of S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) is ⊕_σ ℂ f^σ (multiplicity one for newforms), of dimension [K_f : ℚ] = dim A_f.
acceptance: Fix the Hecke-action convention before identifying differentials; the two choices differ by w_ζ.

sources.locator: Appendix by B. Conrad, p. 68 (printed page; PDF page 72)
sources.match: The cotangent identification and the adjoint warning.

nodes.title: Trivial character: the quotient of J₀(N)
nodes.statement: If χ_f is trivial, let p_f⁰ ⊂ T₀(N) be the kernel of the eigenvalue map on the Hecke algebra of J₀(N). Then A_f⁰ := J₀(N)/p_f⁰J₀(N) is an abelian variety over ℚ of dimension [K_f : ℚ], and the map J₀(N) → J₁(N) (pullback along X₁(N) → X₀(N)) induces an isogeny A_f⁰ → A_f compatible with the K_f-actions.
hypotheses: The pullback J₀(N) → J₁(N) is Hecke-equivariant with finite kernel.
proofSteps: Apply the J₁ argument to J₀(N) with H¹(X₀(N)) free of rank 2 over ℚ ⊗ T₀(N) (same proof as betti-free-rank-two).
The composite J₀(N) → J₁(N) → A_f kills p_f⁰J₀(N) and is nonzero on V_ℓ; compare dimensions.
acceptance: Consumers (EllipticCurveModularity R29.5) use the J₀(N) quotient; keep the isogeny explicit.

nodes.title: Oldforms: A_f inside J₁(M) for N | M
nodes.statement: For N | M, the p_f-isotypic part (for the anemic Hecke algebra of level M) of J₁(M) is isogenous to A_f^{σ₀(M/N)}, embedded through the σ₀(M/N) degeneracy maps J₁(N) → J₁(M) attached to the divisors d | M/N; hence A_f is determined up to isogeny by the eigensystem of f and not by the level at which it is viewed.
hypotheses: The primary source for this multiplicity statement was not read (see coverage).
proofSteps: The oldspace of f at level M is spanned by f(dz), d | M/N (Atkin–Lehner–Li), so the f-part of S₂(Γ₁(M)) has dimension σ₀(M/N)[K_f : ℚ].
The degeneracy maps give J₁(N)^{σ₀(M/N)} → J₁(M), injective up to finite kernel on the f-part (the Ihara-type statement of R14.4 in characteristic zero); compare dimensions.
acceptance: State the multiplicity σ₀(M/N) explicitly; do not identify the level-M quotient with A_f itself.

nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi composite to A_f is nonconstant
nodes.statement: For any rational cusp c of X₁(N) (or ∞ on X₀(N)), the composite X₁(N) → J₁(N) → A_f, x ↦ [x − c] mod p_f, is a nonconstant morphism over ℚ sending c to 0.
hypotheses: A_f ≠ 0; the Abel–Jacobi map and its universal property are Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer F.
proofSteps: The image of a curve under Abel–Jacobi generates its Jacobian; J₁(N) → A_f is surjective with A_f ≠ 0, so the composite cannot be constant.
acceptance: No isogeny to a target curve is asserted here (that is EllipticCurveModularity R29.5).

nodes.title: Hecke operators extend to the Néron model
nodes.statement: T_p^* and (T_p)_* (defined through X₁(N, p) over ℤ[1/Np]) extend uniquely to endomorphisms of the abelian scheme Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/ℤ[1/N]}, so they act on the reduction J_p = Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/F_p} for p ∤ N.
hypotheses: Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/ℤ[1/N]} is an abelian scheme, hence the Néron model of its generic fibre.
proofSteps: Néron mapping property: a homomorphism of generic fibres extends uniquely over ℤ[1/N].
acceptance: The degeneracy maps π_i^{(p)} themselves do not exist over ℤ[1/N] near p; only the induced endomorphisms extend.

sources.locator: Appendix by B. Conrad, p. 72 (printed page; PDF page 76)

nodes.title: The Eichler–Shimura relation
nodes.statement: For p ∤ N, in End_{F_p}(J_p) with J_p = Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/F_p} and F the absolute Frobenius: (T_p)_* = F + ⟨p⟩_* F^∨, and w_ζ⁻¹ F w_ζ = ⟨p⟩_*⁻¹ F.
hypotheses: T₁(N) acts through the Albanese action; F^∨ is the dual (Verschiebung-type) morphism.
proofSteps: Check on a Zariski-dense set of points of X₁(N)_{F̄_p}: over F̄_p the correspondence X₁(N, p) splits into the graph of Frobenius and the transpose of Frobenius twisted by ⟨p⟩ (the Kronecker congruence relation), using p-isogenies of ordinary elliptic curves (Frobenius and Verschiebung).
Pass to Albanese functoriality.
The w_ζ relation follows from the Galois action on ζ (Frobenius sends ζ to ζ^p).
acceptance: The extra w_ζ relation is part of the statement; it is used to identify the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1).

nodes.title: Cusp-normalised Abel–Jacobi maps
nodes.statement: The cusp ∞ ∈ X₀(N)(ℚ) and a ℚ-rational cusp c of X₁(N) (the cusp 0 in the (E, P) moduli model) give Abel–Jacobi morphisms AJ_∞ : X₀(N) → J₀(N), x ↦ [x − ∞], and AJ_c : X₁(N) → J₁(N) over ℚ; they are closed immersions for genus ≥ 1, Hecke-compatible on divisors, and compatible with the degeneracy maps.
hypotheses: Which cusp is rational depends on the moduli model of X₁(N) (µ_N-embedding versus point of exact order N); fix the model before naming the cusp.
proofSteps: Rationality of the cusp from the moduli description of the cusps (R12.3).
Instantiate Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer F's Abel–Jacobi morphism with this base point.
acceptance: No modular parametrisation of an elliptic curve is asserted here.

gaps.title: Oldform multiplicity has no freely available primary source read
gaps.detail: The statement that the f-part of J₁(M) is isogenous to A_f^{σ₀(M/N)} for N | M is standard (Shimura's book, Theorem 7.14 and §7.5; Diamond–Im §6.6), but neither source is freely available and Conrad's appendix does not treat level change. The node records the proof through Atkin–Lehner–Li and the characteristic-zero injectivity of degeneracy maps (R14.4).
